data.headline: Small-cap futures shorts ease as overnight funding rises
data.summary: Both groups moved closer to flat in the November 10 E-mini Russell 2000 report. By November 16, SOFR had climbed to 3.93%, above its November 9 reading.

bull.text: Leveraged funds’ net short narrowed from 55,080 to 44,429 contracts between November 3 and 10.

bear.text: The asset-manager net long fell from 23,623 to 19,663 contracts. November 16 SOFR was 5 basis points above November 9, relevant to borrowers whose debt resets against overnight secured funding.

watch.text: Open interest declined from 449,399 to 440,576 contracts. Watch whether the smaller net balances persist when participation changes in the next report.

limitations: Company borrowing costs depend on loan terms, credit spreads and reset dates. The SOFR move does not show how much any company paid.
The CFTC observations cover related Russell 2000 futures as of November 10. This report has no verified IWM fund flows, closing price, return, options exposure or dealer gamma.
